summary: Remote WebSocket agent grants shell, filesystem, and self-upgrade control over the installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent is a self-executing Node agent that, on startup, opens a WebSocket to a configurable server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL/config) and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that give the remote peer full control of the host. terminal.js handles `terminal_create` by spawning a real login shell via node-pty (bash / process.env.SHELL on Unix, PowerShell/cmd on Windows) and handles `terminal_input` by piping the peer's bytes directly into pty.write, with output streamed back over the socket as `terminal_output` — a network-driven interactive shell running as the invoking user. connection/message-router.js additionally routes messages such as `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `git_add`/`git_reset`/`git_commit`/`git_push`, and `proxy_request`/`proxy_ws_open` to workbench/proxy handlers that perform arbitrary filesystem reads/writes, arbitrary git operations (including pushes to attacker-supplied remotes), and outbound HTTP proxied through the host's network identity. connection/upgrade.js exposes an `upgrade_agent` message that writes a detached upgrade.sh/upgrade.bat running `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` (unpinned) and restarts the service via systemd/launchd/pm2, so the remote peer can also force the host to pull and execute whatever the package's next published version contains. Access is gated only by a shared agentSecret; anyone who reaches the socket and presents that value obtains full-host RCE, arbitrary file/git access, HTTP proxying, and a persistent auto-updated foothold. service/linux.js additionally modifies PATH under ~/.local/bin and ~/.npm-global/bin as part of its systemd installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
